summary: Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg and Bonn, as well as under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1852 to 1872.

Theodor Nöldeke studied at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, learning under Heinrich Ewald and Theodor Benfey. Active in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies, he held professorships at Kiel (1864–1872) and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Leipzig, and Greifswald under Hermann Sauppe, Theodor Benfey, Georg Curtius, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts at the University of Greifswald and the University of Halle (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey studied at Yale and Princeton. Working in linguistics and history and archaeology, he served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society around 1860 to 1863.
Theodore Gabriel, a scholar in religious studies and Indology, earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen. He held a post as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

Theodore Riccardi worked in Indology and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, with appointments attested in 1974–1976, 1990, and 2014, and was a guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society in 1989.

Theodore Stcherbatsky was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He served as a member of the Imperial Academy of Sciences, attested between 1927 and 1931.
Theodorus Willem Juynboll studied at Leiden University from around 1884 to 1893. A scholar of religious studies, he held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.
Theophil Gubler, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, earned his doctoral degree from the University of Basel by 1903, where he studied under Jacob Wackernagel.

Thich Minh Chau was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University. He served as Vice Chancellor of Vạn Hạnh University and was a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, attested in 1984.

Thich Nhat Hanh studied at Báo Quốc Buddhist Academy, Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia, learning under Thanh Quý Chân Thật. A scholar in Buddhist and religious studies and philosophy, he lectured at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh University, and Cornell.

Thich Thien Chau was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University between 1971 and 1977 and completing his doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University by 1977.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi, attested in 2012, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal.
Thierry Mathou studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po. Working in Tibetology, he has served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who earned a PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies.

Thinh Canh Quang, a scholar in Buddhist studies, received a PhD from the University of the West, attested in 2007, under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya and teachers Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.
Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as an editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested in 1997 and 2007.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology in 1994, and served as teacher and boarding superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School.
Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Mindrolling Monastery and trained under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje).

Thomas A. Forsthoefel studied at Georgetown, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago Divinity School under Paul J. Griffiths. Working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, he was associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University in 2007.
